findings.text: Provides a synchronous helper that executes a caller supplied function on a designated CPU through the workqueue facility and returns that function result to the caller. It uses an on stack carrier holding the function pointer plus its argument and a result slot, with a small trampoline that invokes the function and records the outcome.

Exposes CPU hotplug handlers that prepare per CPU pools before use, integrate pools when a CPU comes online, and detach workers when a CPU goes offline. Preparation ensures an initial worker where none exists, while online and offline steps refresh unbound queue placement for the affected processor pod and update node concurrency limits.

Exposes power management entry points that begin a freeze interval, test whether any freezable queue still has activity, and end the interval. Begin and end toggle a global freezing indicator and rebalance every queue concurrency limit, while the busy test reports whether any freezable queue retains active work.

Exposes management of the global unbound CPU set and of the default affinity scope. One path intersects a housekeeping allowance with the requested set and applies on change, another validates and installs a user provided set constrained to possible CPUs, and a parameter interface updates the default scope and refreshes placement for all queues.

Defines a carrier that bundles a work item with a function pointer taking an opaque argument, the argument itself, and a slot for the signed result. The layout lets a synchronous caller wait on the embedded work item and then read back the outcome.

Defines a device wrapper pairing a pointer to the owning workqueue with an embedded generic device object. A container accessor recovers the owning queue from the embedded device, letting sysfs handlers resolve their target queue.

Defines sysfs groupings for workqueues: a common set with identity and concurrency controls, an unbound only set with priority and CPU and scope controls, and a global set with effective and requested and isolated views, all exported under a virtual bus dedicated to workqueues with init time registration.

Requires the global pool mutex for list wide work such as freezing control, hotplug integration and unbound mask changes, and the attach mutex for rebinding or restoring worker affinities. The restore path asserts attach ownership before adjusting unbound workers, while online handling nests attach work inside the global mutex.

Protects per queue attributes with the queue mutex in show paths and with global mutex ownership during attribute preparation, uses read side RCU protection when scanning per queue channels for activity or iterating pools for stall reporting, and requires or acquires the pool spinlock when inspecting busy sets or diagnosing a pool without a running worker.

Distinguishes pool kinds during hotplug: bottom half pools stay untouched, the pool bound to the arriving CPU rebinds its workers, and unbound pools whose allowed set includes the CPU refresh workers against allowed intersected with online CPUs. Offline handling detaches local workers, clears the online mark, and likewise refreshes pod placement and node limits for unbound queues.

Models freeze as a global flag with three phases: begin warns if already freezing, sets the flag and rebalances limits; busy is only meaningful while set and reports activity in freezable queues; thaw clears the flag when set and rebalances again, doing nothing when freezing was not active.

Applying a new unbound set skips bound queues and queues being destroyed, prepares per queue change contexts and either commits all of them or abandons on first error while always releasing contexts. On success it publishes the new set, forces detached rescuers to reevaluate affinity, and rebinds workers in disassociated per CPU pools.

Housekeeping updates allocate a temporary mask, prefer the intersection of the requested unbound set with the housekeeping set and fall back to the requested set when empty, apply only on change, and on success record the complement of housekeeping within possible CPUs as the isolated set.

Sysfs stores validate strictly: concurrency limit must be a positive integer, priority must fall within system nice bounds, CPU sets must parse, scope names must match a known scope, and strictness must be numeric with nonzero treated as true. Visibility restricts concurrency control to read only for bottom half or ordered queues, and scope display annotates the default choice with its current resolution.

Provides sysfs show and store handlers for per queue identity, concurrency limit, priority, CPU set, scope and strictness, plus global handlers for effective and requested and isolated masks, and a device release handler that frees the wrapper. Preparation duplicates current attributes under global mutex ownership for later validated application, and global mask display serializes under the same mutex.

Preparation fails cleanly when worker creation fails, offline handling warns and aborts when invoked away from the departing CPU, unbound restoration warns if affinity adjustment fails, housekeeping and global mask stores fail on mask allocation shortage, and freeze misuse or negative activity counts trigger one time warnings.

Watchdog configuration starts with a thirty second threshold, a repeating timer object, global and per CPU touch marks initialized to the boot time base, and separate panic controls for repeated stalls and for single long stalls, the latter starting disabled.

Models stall detection as a periodic scan that ignores empty pools and disabled thresholds, compares each pool last progress mark against the freshest touch mark, rechecks under the pool lock before declaring a stall, flags per CPU non bottom half pools for deeper diagnosis, reports all queues, emits busy worker traces, escalates through counter and duration based panic policy, then refreshes touch marks and rearms the timer.

Stall reporting defers console output to avoid deadlock with drivers that queue work while holding console related locks, snapshots the pool CPU under lock for safe post unlock use, skips cross CPU tracing when the stalled CPU is offline to avoid unacknowledged interrupts, and relies on the pool lock to keep the last woken worker reference valid during diagnosis.

Defines user visible identities: the virtual bus uses the workqueue name, per queue controls cover per CPU mode and concurrency limit and priority and CPU set and affinity scope and strictness, global controls cover effective and requested and isolated CPU sets, the watchdog interval defaults to thirty seconds, and special ordered or bottom half queues restrict concurrency control to read only.
